findings.title: [P2] Verify file contents rather than Git status entries
findings.body: The before/after porcelain comparison does not detect changes to files that were already modified: appending to an existing dirty file leaves the same ` M path` entry, so the probe passes despite changing the main tree. Detached worktrees also share repository configuration; a probe can run `git config --local core.hooksPath /tmp/probe-hooks` without changing porcelain output. Consequently, repository code executed by a probe can persist changes while this integrity check reports success. The research scope check in `chart-ticket.sh` has the same dirty-file blind spot. Enforce write isolation, or compare content hashes and separately protect shared Git metadata.

findings.cross_file_justification: The agent definition grants an unrestricted Write tool plus WebFetch; .claude/data/agent-types.yaml marks it write_capable: true; the only mechanical enforcement of the 'write exactly one file' rule is the post-hoc git-status diff in chart-ticket.sh op_research_end (lines 451-471), which detects but never reverts.
findings.description: chart-researcher fetches arbitrary web pages (WebFetch) and holds a Write tool with no path restriction. The 'write exactly one file under grimoires/loa/research/' rule is prompt-only. A prompt-injected researcher can overwrite any repository file, including .claude/hooks/safety/*.sh, .claude/settings or CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md. chart-ticket.sh research-end only runs after the subagent returns, compares `git status` snapshots and exits 1; it does not restore the files. A rewritten PreToolUse hook is therefore executed by the parent session's next Bash call before anyone has a chance to revert, and the parent command doc (chart.md) advertises the skill as having 'no App-Zone write path'.
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted web content steers the researcher into a Write outside the report path; the change persists and executes (hooks, settings, instruction files) before research-end flags it. Detection after the fact is not a boundary.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the researcher's Write to the single report path mechanically (a PreToolUse hook on Write for agent chart-researcher that denies any path other than grimoires/loa/research/chart-<slug>-<ticket>.md), or drop Write and have the parent session write the report from the subagent's final message. In research-end, on failure also `git checkout --` / delete the offending paths and refuse to continue the session until the operator reviews.

findings.description: chart-unblock-probe.sh is documented as 'the only way a decision:unblock ticket runs anything' and its verdict is 'exit 1 when the main tree's status changed'. The verdict is computed solely from `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching` before and after. That check cannot see: (1) anything under $MAIN/.git (the worktree shares it, so `git config core.hooksPath`, `core.fsmonitor`, a new .git/hooks/* file or .git/info/exclude edits are invisible and give persistent code execution on the operator's next git command); (2) edits to files that were already modified or already untracked before the probe (the status line is identical, so the content change is undetected, e.g. an already-dirty grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml); (3) anything outside the repository (~/.ssh, ~/.claude, ~/.bashrc, other checkouts). The probe runs with the operator's full privileges, PATH, env and network.
findings.failure_mode: A probe command (agent-authored, possibly steered by injected content from the question it is probing) persists changes via .git/config or hooks, or modifies an already-dirty tracked file, and the helper reports 'main tree unchanged' exit 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare content, not status: snapshot `git stash create`/`git write-tree` of the index+worktree hash and a sha256 of each untracked file before and after; additionally hash $MAIN/.git/config, .git/hooks and .git/info before/after and fail on any change. Run the probe with GIT_DIR/GIT_COMMON_DIR unset and `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null` in a worktree created from a separate clone, or at least set `git config --worktree` isolation and HOME to a scratch dir. Document that this is a fence, not a sandbox, as the SP-1 comment does.

findings.description: The research scope check derives 'bad' from `comm -13` of two git-status listings and whitelists every path under grimoires/loa/research/. Gaps: a tracked file that was already ' M' at research-begin can be rewritten by the subagent with no change in its status line, so it never appears in `bad`; the whole research/ directory is exempt, so the subagent may overwrite other tickets' reports, other maps' reports, or plant a new grimoires/loa/research/chart-<slug>-<anything>.md; the .chart-*-*.dispatch markers themselves live there and can be deleted/forged by the subagent to lift the 5-dispatch cap in research-begin. Only the first line of the expected report is validated.
findings.failure_mode: A misbehaving researcher modifies already-dirty tracked files or other research reports and research-end returns the report path with exit 0, so the session treats the run as in-scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Record content hashes (e.g. `git stash create` tree hash plus sha256 of untracked files) at research-begin and compare at research-end; narrow the allowlist to exactly ${RESEARCH}/chart-${SLUG}-${TICKET}.md; store dispatch markers outside the directory the subagent may write (e.g. .run/ or $TMPDIR) and compare their mtime/content.

findings.cross_file_justification: op_handoff writes grimoires/loa/context/chart-<slug>.md; plan-and-analyze.md (new context_files entry, priority 1, 'settled decisions, confirm, do not re-ask') ingests it as top-priority PRD input.
findings.description: The hand-off snapshot inlines every file matching grimoires/loa/research/chart-<slug>-*.md, not only reports for tickets that exist on the map, and then hands the whole document to /plan-and-analyze as priority-1 'settled' context. Report content originates from WebFetch (external, attacker-controlled) and from a subagent whose write scope is not mechanically bounded (SEC-001/003). The L6 sanitizer and the UNTRUSTED banner reduce but do not eliminate the risk: a planted or poisoned report rides into the PRD with higher trust than any other context, and the snapshot header literally instructs the consumer not to question its contents.
findings.failure_mode: Injected text in a fetched source lands in a report, is inlined into the snapshot, and is read by /plan-and-analyze as a settled decision rather than data; the PRD inherits attacker-chosen requirements.
findings.suggested_fix: Inline only reports whose <ticket> matches a ledger row with source map:<slug>/<ticket>; link (do not inline) the report body in the snapshot, or inline only the `## Options` and `## Sources` sections after sanitizing; have /plan-and-analyze treat the 'Research reports' section as untrusted data explicitly, separate from the settled ledger rows.

findings.description: FR-1.1 blocks `git branch -D` to prevent loss of unmerged work. The new exception lets a spike/<slug> branch be force-deleted when grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml contains a row with status decided, source grimoires/loa/spikes/<slug>.md and a transition with by starting 'operator:'. That ledger is an ordinary tracked YAML file the agent can author with the Write tool (bypassing dec-write-lib.sh entirely), so the 'operator decided' signal is a string the agent controls. The hook does not verify the spike branch is pushed to a remote (the design claims spikes are 'pushed, never merged'), so a never-pushed spike with the only copy of the prototype can be deleted after a self-authored ledger edit.
findings.failure_mode: Agent writes a decided row with by: operator:x into decisions.yaml, then runs `git branch -D spike/<slug>`; the safety hook allows it and unpushed spike commits are lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Additionally require that the branch tip is reachable from a remote-tracking ref (`git branch -r --contains refs/heads/spike/<slug>`), and/or require the ledger row to be committed on HEAD (`git show HEAD:grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml`) rather than read from the working tree, so an uncommitted Write cannot flip the gate.

findings.description: san1 strips control characters so each appended bullet is one line, but section_append passes the text to awk via `-v line=...`. awk processes backslash escapes in -v assignments, so a value containing the two characters `\n` becomes a real newline in the map doc. --line, --name, --why and the bead title (from br) can therefore inject additional lines into grimoires/loa/maps/<slug>.md, including a forged '- X (DEC-0001, bd-y): ...' decision bullet or a new '## ' heading that shifts section boundaries used by section_bullets/remaining_hint/handoff gating. Same applies to set_status via -v s.
findings.failure_mode: A crafted argument or bead title yields multi-line, structurally different map doc content despite the one-line sanitizer, misleading the fog/frontier checks and the hand-off snapshot.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the text through the environment (`line="$2" awk '... ENVIRON["line"] ...'`) or strip backslashes in san1; validate that the appended bullet contains no newline after awk processing.
